issues.description: The problem statement explicitly requires calculateTotalPrice to be a static method, but the provided solution implements calculateTotalPrice as an instance (non-static) method. This mismatch between the specification and the solution can confuse students about whether to implement the method as static and may cause inconsistency with tests or instructor expectations.
issues.suggestedFix: Either update the solution to declare calculateTotalPrice as static (public static int calculateTotalPrice(Meal meal) { ... }) so it matches the problem statement, or revise the problem statement to remove the requirement that calculateTotalPrice be static and state that it should be an instance method. Ensure both the specification and reference implementation use the same static/non-static designation.

issues.description: The problem text instructs students to initialize the SealSaloon attributes (orders and stock) in the constructor but also requires the stock attribute to be static. Initializing a static field in an instance constructor is contradictory: static fields are class-level and are not typically initialized per-instance. The solution initializes stock as a static final field at declaration, which conflicts with the earlier instruction to initialize it in the constructor. This inconsistency can confuse students about where and how to initialize the shared stock.
issues.suggestedFix: Clarify the problem statement: if stock is intended to be shared across all SealSaloon instances, instruct students to declare and initialize it as a static field (for example, private static final Stock stock = new Stock();). If instead stock should be per-instance and initialized in the constructor, remove the static requirement. Make the specification and any example/solution consistent.
